blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — APO Production Unit Inc., the printing agency for Philippine passports, clarified on Wednesday that it did not request an increase in passport fees. Instead, its president, Atty. Gil Carlos Puyat, told the Senate finance subcommittee that the agency had asked for a government subsidy to offset passport printing costs without passing the burden on to the public. Senate finance panel chairperson Sen. JV Ejercito inquired about the reported passport fee increase, expressing concern over the public’s expenses as well as the cost of producing passports.
